results.name: high_alternation_pair_choice_rate
results.description: Among trials where both sequences have alternation rate >= 0.6 and the rates differ, the proportion choosing the MORE alternating sequence; observed above the null means people penalise over-alternation less than the model's quadratic ideal-rate term implies, below means they penalise it more.

results.name: run_length_variety_choice_rate
results.description: Among trials where the two sequences have the same alternation rate but a different number of distinct run lengths, the proportion choosing the sequence with MORE distinct run lengths; observed above the null means people prize irregular run structure beyond what the model's alternation/imbalance/streak/symmetry terms capture, below means they prefer regular run structure more than the model predicts.

results.name: overall_left_choice_rate
results.description: Overall proportion of trials on which the left sequence was chosen; observed above the null means people have a left-side bias the model (which has no side term) under-produces, below means a right-side bias.

results.name: participant_majority_agreement_sd
results.description: SD across participants of each person's rate of agreeing with the pair-wise majority choice (majority from the same dataset, tied pairs skipped); observed above the null means people still differ in consistency more than the model's person-level sensitivity and lapse rates produce, below means the model over-produces individual differences.
results.code:
# name: participant_majority_agreement_sd
# description: SD across participants of each person's rate of agreeing with the pair-wise majority choice (majority from the same dataset, tied pairs skipped); observed above the null means people still differ in consistency more than the model's person-level sensitivity and lapse rates produce, below means the model over-produces individual differences.
def test_statistic(df):
    a = df["sequence_a"].to_numpy().astype(str); b = df["sequence_b"].to_numpy().astype(str)
    first = np.where(a < b, a, b)
    key = pd.Series(np.char.add(np.char.add(first, "|"), np.where(a < b, b, a)))
    chose_first = (np.where(df["chose_left"].to_numpy() == 1, a, b) == first).astype(float)
    rate = pd.Series(chose_first).groupby(key).transform("mean").to_numpy()
    ok = rate != 0.5
    agree = np.where(rate > 0.5, chose_first, 1 - chose_first)
    s = pd.Series(agree[ok]).groupby(df["participant_id"].to_numpy()[ok]).mean()
    return float(s.std())

results.name: shorter_max_run_by_one_choice_rate
results.description: Among trials where the two sequences' longest runs differ by exactly one flip, the proportion choosing the sequence with the SHORTER longest run; observed above the null means a one-flip-longer streak hurts more than the model's linear longest-run share (plus alternation) implies, below means it hurts less.

results.name: alternation_preference_participant_sd
results.description: SD across participants of each person's rate of choosing the more alternating sequence (trials where alternation rates differ); observed above the null means people differ in the direction/strength of their switching preference more than the model's personal ideal rates and sensitivities produce, below means the model over-produces that heterogeneity.

results.name: low_alternation_pair_choice_rate
results.description: Among trials where both sequences have alternation rate <= 0.5 and the rates differ, the proportion choosing the MORE alternating sequence; observed above the null means people reward extra switching among streaky sequences more strongly than the model's quadratic term implies, below means less.

results.name: near_chance_participant_fraction
results.description: Fraction of participants whose agreement with the pair-wise majority choice is below 0.6 (near-chance responders; majority from the same dataset, ties skipped); observed above the null means the data hold more disengaged/idiosyncratic people than the model's lapse and sensitivity distributions produce, below means the model over-produces them.

# name: near_chance_participant_fraction
# description: Fraction of participants whose agreement with the pair-wise majority choice is below 0.6 (near-chance responders; majority from the same dataset, ties skipped); observed above the null means the data hold more disengaged/idiosyncratic people than the model's lapse and sensitivity distributions produce, below means the model over-produces them.
def test_statistic(df):
    a = df["sequence_a"].to_numpy().astype(str); b = df["sequence_b"].to_numpy().astype(str)
    first = np.where(a < b, a, b)
    key = pd.Series(np.char.add(np.char.add(first, "|"), np.where(a < b, b, a)))
    chose_first = (np.where(df["chose_left"].to_numpy() == 1, a, b) == first).astype(float)
    rate = pd.Series(chose_first).groupby(key).transform("mean").to_numpy()
    ok = rate != 0.5
    agree = np.where(rate > 0.5, chose_first, 1 - chose_first)
    s = pd.Series(agree[ok]).groupby(df["participant_id"].to_numpy()[ok]).mean()
    return float((s < 0.6).mean())
